pages.name: The Founding — the Making of the Peoples

text.markdown:
The Word made one people; mortals made the rest. When The Light seeded the prime world (Ch. 1), it set upon it a single willed people — call them the base stock, the first humanity. The many species that fill the world today — the slender and beautiful, the towering and tireless, the compact and unbreakable — are not separate creations of the Word. They are engineered: designed roughly a thousand years ago (or more) by the mortal powers of a lost high-corporate age — the ancestor-corporations, the forerunners of today's Ten — who learned to rewrite the seeded stock and made of it a catalogue of castes. This is the setting's founding act of mortal hubris, and it rhymes forward through everything: the peoples remade themselves by artifice long before anyone bolted chrome to a spine or opened a channel in the Wired.
- Engineered as castes, not as gifts. Each species was built for a purpose the ancestor-corps wanted filled, most of the eight playable species are engineered Homo sapiens subspecies (Homo sapiens gracilis, fossor, giganticus, and so on), a detail corp geneticists still record in the Linnaean binomial. The three clearest cases:
- The Elvani (“elves,” Homo sapiens gracilis) — the aesthetic caste, designed as an upper-class distinction: slender, striking, unnervingly graceful, slow to age, engineered to be seen in the boardroom, the media suite, and the pleasure-tiers. A bespoke aristocracy the old wealthy could literally commission. Their beauty and poise are engineered traits, not magic — a fact they are content to let others forget.
- The Corran (“squats,” Homo sapiens fossor) — the labor caste, built compact, immensely strong, and hardy to work the deep mines and the cramped service crawls no baseline human could survive. The corps still read them as “just labor.”
- The Goliar (“ogres,” Homo sapiens giganticus) — the heavy caste, towering muscle engineered for hazardous industry, demolition, and enforcement — still deployed as breachers and riot-line and still underestimated as “just grunts.”

The class system of the modern hive (Ch. 6) is the fossil of this genetic caste system: the strata were literally designed before they were ever built in steel. (Pure Humans — Homo sapiens basalis — remain the base stock the Word seeded; Changers, Mutants, Revenants, and Cyborgs are made, not bred — see below.)
- Castes became peoples. Over a thousand years the engineered lines bred true — and, by design or accident, cannot interbreed with one another (the universal genetic-incompatibility rule: cross-species unions are common and socially normal but never produce children, so there are no born half-species). Each line scattered, married within itself, and grew into a genuine culture — the Elvani with their salons, patron-houses, and exacting social codes; the Corran with their guild-clans, dialects, and long memory; the Goliar with their kinship-crews and plain-spoken loyalty. A person today is not a product; they are the descendant of one, which is a very different and much more human thing. The vanity caste became a nation, the labor castes became nations, and none of them asked to be born to the role their makers intended. The mutual contempt is already canon: the Elvani look down on the Corran as brute labor, and the Corran return it with interest.
- The made, not the bred. Four of the eight are not engineered breeds at all but conditions laid over a living person: Changers (metamorphic strains), Mutant Humans (mutagenic corruption), Revenants (embodied undead), and Cyborgs (Machina sapiens — machine-first beings no longer legally or biologically “human”). They are made within a single lifetime, not descended from the Founding — the Founding explains the bred peoples; these are what the world does to individuals now.
- Known, but normalized. This is not a hidden truth waiting to be uncovered. Every educated person knows the ancestries were made in the Founding, the way we know about fallen empires — it is ancient, settled history, not a corporate secret. What is live is what it means now: who is “refined” and who is “stock,” who deserves the Crown and who was built for the Sinks, whose ancestors commissioned and whose were commissioned. The prejudice is the more insidious for being dressed as heritage rather than hatred.
- Reconciled with the cosmology. The Founding does not violate Ch. 1. The Dark One cannot create, only deface — but mortals, made in a creating world, can shape what the Word already spoke. Engineering a people is not damnation and not the Dark's work; it is artistry and pride, morally neutral in itself, exactly like chrome (Ch. 5). It becomes the Dark's road only where it reaches toward domination and un-speaking — which is precisely the shadow lying over the elven aristocracy and the corps that still trade in “who was built better.”
- The Mutants, re-read. This casts Ch. 5's Mutants in a colder light: some Mutant lines are not only taint bred true but failed, abandoned, or corrupted branches of the same old engineering — castes that broke, experiments the ancestor-corps discarded, or lines the Incursion (Ch. 3) later got into. The hive's tainted underclass is, in part, the wreckage of the Founding no one wants to admit authorship of.

text.markdown:
Eight kindreds, engineered or made, each a people with memory, pride, and contempt.

### Pure Humans — The Base Stock

![Pure Humans - the base stock](modules/draw-steel-ghostwire/docs/manuscript/print-art/species/pure-human.png)

*Pure Humans - the base stock — Ghostwire AI (AI-generated)*

Names: Homo sapiens basalis · Baseline Human · Norms, Naturals, Purebloods, flatlines. Kind: bred (the seeded stock — the one people the Word actually made; Ch. 1). Origin & nature. Pure Humans are the original people — the single willed stock The Light seeded on the prime world before any mortal hand rewrote it (Ch. 1, the Founding). Every other bred species is a variation the ancestor-corps cut from this cloth; every made condition is most often laid over a human body. They carry no engineered caste-purpose, no undead grave-pull, no mutagenic taint, no machine chassis — which is precisely their identity: the unmodified default, the widest-open build, the point of comparison for everyone else. Their gift is adaptability (the Adaptive Edge): no single thing they do best, and nothing they cannot learn.

Culture & place in the world. Humans remain the demographic majority and the assumed "standard citizen" around whom the megacities, their products, their SINs, and their laws are all designed — the default the corporate world quietly builds for. This is both privilege and trap: a human is normal and therefore invisible, neither prized like an Elvan nor feared like a Goliar nor owned outright like a Cyborg, free to disappear into the crowd of a hundred million. That very ordinariness makes them the setting's great swing vote in the Cosmic War. The least visibly altered by the war, they make the ideal vessel, agent, convert, or victim — the Light recruits them, the Dark tempts them, and the corps spend them. Most runners are human for the simplest reason: humans are who the world overlooks.

### Cyborgs — The Machine-First

![Cyborgs - the machine-first](modules/draw-steel-ghostwire/docs/manuscript/print-art/species/cyborg.png)

*Cyborgs - the machine-first — Ghostwire AI (AI-generated)*

Names: Machina sapiens (deliberately outside genus Homo — machine-first, no longer legally or biologically "human") · Full-Conversion Cyborg · Borgs, Chrome, Tin-men, Husks. Kind: made (a total conversion of a once-living person; not a bred people). Origin & nature. A Cyborg is the far end of the chrome road. A cyber-augmented human bolts implants onto a living human chassis and stays human (Ch. 12); a Cyborg has spent all of their Body Integrity — the artificial chassis no longer overlays the person, it replaces them. Whether by catastrophic injury salvaged into a frame, corporate conversion of an asset, or a soul's own hunger for the machine, the result is a being that runs on modules and mag-servos, healed by medtech and Technomancer resonance rather than rest or medicine. They do not scale by growing flesh; they scale by slotting hardware.

The severed thing. Full conversion cuts the Cyborg off from the one source. They can never touch magic — arcane, divine, elemental, resonant, infernal, holy — because in the locked cosmology all magic is a mortal reaching for the Word (Ch. 2, the one-source rule), and a machine-first being has no living aperture left to reach with. This is the setting's starkest statement that the soul is not in the parts: you can rebuild the body to the last gram and still sever it from the Signal. It is also why the Cyborg is existentially unstable — emotionally damped, capped in Presence, and prone at zero Stamina to System Crisis, a psychosis-rage the Director drives until it burns out or the frame is destroyed. Culture & place in the world. Cyborgs are feared as inhuman, prized as assets, claimed as property, and — by a growing few — revered as the next stage of the species. They live the setting's central question of whether soul, machine identity, and divine or infernal influence can share one body. Frames give them their working castes: the Warframe (heavy combat chassis), the Infiltrator (stealth/insertion), and the Medtech (field repair and surgery); two further frames are held in reserve. A Cyborg on a crew is muscle and hardware that magic cannot mend — and a soul the war is fighting over from a strange, cold distance.

### Changers — The Skin-Turners

![Changers - the skin-turners](modules/draw-steel-ghostwire/docs/manuscript/print-art/species/changer.png)

*Changers - the skin-turners — Ghostwire AI (AI-generated)*

Names: Homo sapiens versipellis ("skin-turner") · Metamorphic Type · Changers, Shifters, skins, weres. Kind: made (a metamorphic strain, not a Founding caste — one species with internal lines). Origin & nature. Changers are one species braided from three possible roots: engineered animal hybridization (corp bio-labs splicing beast into human), occult shapeshifting strains (old were-lineages the war stirred back to life), and dimensional morphic contamination (flesh that touched a thinning membrane and learned to run). Whatever the root, every Changer shares the Alternate Form birthright — a human-passing form, an overtly bestial hybrid combat form, and a full beast form — and a Feral Tell, some animal marker (eyes, gait, teeth, scent) that the passing form can minimize but never fully erase. They cannot be surprised while aware; they are also baited through that Tell.

The lines. Changers run in subtype families, each a different animal instinct made flesh: the Wolf (pack hunter — strength and the hunt), the Rat (survivor and infiltrator — the gutter's own), the Feline (ambush predator — the pounce from the dark), the Reptile (cold endurance — the patient coil), and the Avian (scout and skirmisher — the eye from on high). Two more families are held in reserve. Culture & place in the world. Changers do not have one culture; they have as many as they have lines and origins, bound by a shared experience of not quite passing. In the megacities a Changer is a walking contradiction — human enough to hold a SIN, beast enough to be hunted when the Tell shows — so many run in tight kin-packs that blur the line between family, gang, and hunting party. Some corps prize engineered Changers as living infiltration and tracking assets; the occult and dimensional strains are more often feared as monsters or courted as recruits by both sides of the war. On a crew a Changer is versatility incarnate: the face who becomes the scout who becomes the beast that ends the fight.

### Revenants — The Undying

![Revenants - the undying](modules/draw-steel-ghostwire/docs/manuscript/print-art/species/revenant.png)

*Revenants - the undying — Ghostwire AI (AI-generated)*

Names: Homo mortuus redivivus · Reanimate / Post-Mortem Type · Revs, Deaders, Rotters, Ghosts (late-stage). Kind: made (no one is born a Revenant — they are the returned dead). Origin & nature. No one starts life as a Revenant. They are made in the moment of death: a person who died with a purpose too fierce to release — vengeance, an oath, a debt, a flat refusal — and rose again, sustained by will rather than blood, keeping the memories and personality of the life they left. In this setting the Cosmic War supercharges that return: the Light may send a soul back to finish holy work, the Dark One may deny a soul its rest out of spite, or a corp's resurrection-tech may fail in a way that is really something older reaching through the tear. A Revenant begins as embodied undead and only slowly loses the flesh.

The Decay and the dread. A Revenant's body is a countdown. Over a career they walk a Decay ladder — from Fleshbound (a rotting, cold-fleshed corpse that walks) to Withered/Skeletal (dried toward hardened bone) to Spectral (translucent, phasing, ghostlike) — trading a little humanity at each rung for a little more of the grave's power, until the late-stage Revenant is nearly a wraith. Their Undying Return means a felled Revenant does not die but drops inert and rises again after a respite — which makes them relentless, and terrifying to fight. But it is not true immortality: fire taken while inert, consecrated or annihilating force meant to lay the dead to rest, or the deliberate destruction of the inert body ends them for good. This is why fire is a Revenant's oldest fear, and why an enemy who knows what they are facing brings a torch. Culture & place in the world. Revenants have no homeland and no bloodline — they are recruited from every other people by death itself — so their "culture" is one of purpose and unfinished business. They are walking proof that in this war death is not final, which makes them holy to some Light-orders (a soul granted a second chance) and abominations to others (a thing that should be laid to rest); the Dark One's cults covet them as recruits already halfway across. Corps that dabble in resurrection-tech both create them and hunt them. Every Revenant is a story with its last chapter unwritten — the ideal crew member with a reason, and the ideal antagonist who will not stop coming.

### Mutants — The Marked

![Mutants - the marked](modules/draw-steel-ghostwire/docs/manuscript/print-art/species/mutant.png)

*Mutants - the marked — Ghostwire AI (AI-generated)*

Names: Homo sapiens aberrans · Aberrant / Mutagenic Type · Muties, Tainted, Wrongborn. Kind: made or born-marked — but never a clean bred people; always carries the taint. (See also Ch. 5, corruption, and the Founding note that some Mutant lines are failed or discarded engineered stock.) Origin & nature. A Mutant is human clay the world has rewritten — by inherited taint, by a birth in a corrupted zone, by a magical accident, an infernal bargain, or deliberate corp gene-forging. Born or made, there is no difference: every mutation is, at root, a wound the world left in a body that the body turned into a weapon. Some Mutant strains are older than any individual — the Founding note is explicit that a fraction of Mutant-kind are failed, discarded, or corrupted lines of the same thousand-year-old engineering that made the Elvani beautiful and the Corran strong: castes that came out wrong, and were culled or cast into the

Sinks to breed among themselves. Others are freshly touched last week. All of them share one thing. The Corruptive Flaw. Every Mutant carries a permanent Corruptive Flaw — the price of their power, and the setting's clearest fingerprint of the Dark One on ordinary flesh. The Flaw deepens as the Mutant leans into their gifts (a hidden Corruption Load that rises with every serious mutation), scaling from a Latent quirk, to a Manifest visible burden, to an Ascendant danger where the Dark's hand shows openly and control itself must be rolled for. This is the tragic engine of the species: power and corruption are the same current, and the more a Mutant reaches for one the more they drink of the other. A Mutant is never just a monster — most are victims of a war fought across generations, bearing a stain they never chose. Culture & place in the world. Mutants are feared as monsters, hunted as threats, hidden by their own kind in undercity enclaves, or forged on purpose by corps as expendable bio-assets — and where they stand in society tracks almost exactly with how visible and how deep their taint runs. Loose strains (Brute, Aberrant, Tainted, Latent) give them concept-families rather than true castes, because mutation is chaotic by nature and refuses to be sorted. The Dark One's cults revere powerful Mutants as chosen vessels; Light-orders meet them with pity, suspicion, or crusading steel. On a crew a Mutant is raw, escalating power with a cost the whole table can see coming — the friend who is always one bargain away from becoming the thing they fight.

### Elvani — The Aesthetic Caste

![Elvani - the aesthetic caste](modules/draw-steel-ghostwire/docs/manuscript/print-art/species/elvani.png)

*Elvani - the aesthetic caste — Ghostwire AI (AI-generated)*

Names: Homo sapiens gracilis ("slender/graceful") · Aesthetic-Class Engineered Type · Elves, corp-dolls, Prettyboys, Pointers, Highborn. Kind: bred (a Founding caste; breeds true, cannot interbreed). Origin & nature. The ancestor-corps engineered the Elvani to be seen: the faces of the boardroom, the media suite, the diplomatic table, and the pleasure-tiers — a bespoke aristocracy the old wealthy could literally commission. Slender, striking, unnervingly graceful, quick, commanding, and slow to age, they were the vanity caste made flesh. A thousand years on they are a fully distinct people with their own high culture — salons, patron-houses, exacting social codes — and one crucial, deliberate truth: their beauty and charm are engineered, not magical. An Elvan's "glamor" is poise and pheromone and perfect bearing, not sorcery; they cast no better than anyone, and they are happy to let others forget the difference. Their

signature is Ephemeral Grace — the twinned gift of a charm that lands like truth and a body that nothing quite catches. Long-lived, not deathless. The Elvani are Ageless in the engineered sense: their physiology resists aging and preserves youth for centuries. They are not immortal — violence, disease, drain, and eventually extreme old age still take them, and they die like anyone else; they simply take a very long time to do it (contrast the Revenant's made undeath, Ch. 15, which is the only true "deathlessness," and even that ends in fire). A several-hundred-year lifespan is advantage enough: an Elvan can outwait a rival's whole career, and — because they breed true and forget nothing — an Elvani grudge or debt can outlast the humans who first incurred it. Culture & place in the world. The Elvani sit at the top of the corporate social ladder and are never quite allowed to forget who put them there: adored and objectified, elevated and owned, a status symbol before a person. That gilded cage breeds patron intrigue, blackmail-webs dressed as salons, and the occasional beautiful runner who walks away from everything the world told them they were for. Their contempt for the Corran as "brute labor" is canon and mutual — the two engineered castes, cut from the same act a thousand years apart in station, despise each other on sight. The overtly Elvani conglomerate is Argent Exchange (Ch. 8), where this whole caste-legacy becomes present-day corporate power. A disgraced or discarded Elvan is fertile ground for the Dark One's whisper that real freedom is power, not patronage.

### Corran — The Labor Caste

![Corran - the labor caste](modules/draw-steel-ghostwire/docs/manuscript/print-art/species/corran.png)

*Corran - the labor caste — Ghostwire AI (AI-generated)*

Names: Homo sapiens fossor ("delver/digger") · Corran / Labor-Class Engineered Type · Squats, Deepers, dust-eaters. Kind: bred (a Founding caste; breeds true, cannot interbreed). Origin & nature. The ancestor-corps engineered the Corran as the laborer breed — compact, immensely strong and hardy, built to work the deep mines, the cramped service crawls, the high-pressure and low-clearance spaces machines couldn't reach and baseline humans couldn't survive. They read as dwarves in build and constitution but stripped of the old fantasy trappings: no universal beards, no rune-magic birthright — just Corran men and women, proud and practical, engineered to endure and not go down. Their signature is Unyielding: the immovable laborer who refuses to be pushed, pulled, knocked down, or budged.

Culture & place in the world. A thousand years on the Corran are a fully distinct people with their own communities, dialects, and above all guild-clans — the tight, loyal work-crew-families that double as information networks and safehouse chains a crew ignores at its peril. The megacorps still read them as low-class — "just labor" — and the Corran repay it with deep solidarity, a very long memory, and a chip on the shoulder the size of a mine cart. Because they breed true and forget nothing, a Corran feud or debt runs for generations. They sit at the bottom of the corp class ladder and know it, which makes them natural runners, union agitators, undercity power-brokers, and reluctant heroes with real grievances — and fertile recruiting ground for both a Light-faith that prizes endurance and loyalty, and a Dark One who offers power to the perpetually overlooked. Their mutual contempt with the Elvani (Ch. 17) is a ready-made table tension.

### Goliar — The Heavy Caste

![Goliar - the heavy caste](modules/draw-steel-ghostwire/docs/manuscript/print-art/species/goliar.png)

*Goliar - the heavy caste — Ghostwire AI (AI-generated)*

Names: Homo sapiens giganticus ("giant") · Goliar / Heavy-Class Engineered Type · Ogres, slabs, Wallbreakers, Big-uns, Grunts. Kind: bred (a Founding caste; breeds true, cannot interbreed). Origin & nature. The ancestor-corps engineered the Goliar as the heavy breed — towering slabs of muscle built for hazardous heavy industry, demolition, load-bearing, and security/enforcement work no baseline human could survive and no Corran was big enough to do. Where the Corran are compact and unbreakable, the Goliar are enormous and overpowering — the most physically front-loaded people in the world. Their signature is Towering Menace: large size and long reach, crushing might, and a bulk so intimidating it turns their blunt manner into fear-based social power.

Culture & place in the world. A thousand years on the Goliar are a fully distinct people with their own communities, kinship-crews, and a hard-won culture of loyalty, plain speech, and slow-burning pride. The corps still deploy them as muscle — bouncers, breachers, bodyguards, riot-line — and still underestimate them as "just grunts," mistaking a slow tongue for a slow mind, which is a mistake made exactly once. Their loyalty runs deep and their memory of who treated them like people and who treated them like equipment runs deeper — fertile ground for both the Light's message of dignity and the Dark One's promise of power to the used-up. A Goliar crew-boss commands a respect no corp badge can buy, and their plain-spoken honesty in a world of liars makes them either the most trusted member of a crew or the one who never sees the double-cross coming. The sight of an angry Goliar coming through the wall ends most negotiations early.

This is the setting's starkest statement that the soul is not in the parts: you can rebuild the body to the last gram and still sever it from the Signal. It is also why the Cyborg is existentially unstable — emotionally damped, capped in Presence, and prone at zero Stamina to System Crisis, a psychosis-rage the Director drives until it burns out or the frame is destroyed. Culture & place in the world. Cyborgs are feared as inhuman, prized as assets, claimed as property, and — by a growing few — revered as the next stage of the species. They live the setting's central question of whether soul, machine identity, and divine or infernal influence can share one body. Frames give them their working castes: the Warframe (heavy combat chassis), the Infiltrator (stealth/insertion), and the Medtech (field repair and surgery); two further frames are held in reserve. A Cyborg on a crew is muscle and hardware that magic cannot mend — and a soul the war is fighting over from a strange, cold distance.

Changers — The Skin-Turners

Changers - the skin-turners — Ghostwire AI (AI-generated)

Names: Homo sapiens versipellis ("skin-turner") · Metamorphic Type · Changers, Shifters, skins, weres. Kind: made (a metamorphic strain, not a Founding caste — one species with internal lines). Origin & nature. Changers are one species braided from three possible roots: engineered animal hybridization (corp bio-labs splicing beast into human), occult shapeshifting strains (old were-lineages the war stirred back to life), and dimensional morphic contamination (flesh that touched a thinning membrane and learned to run). Whatever the root, every Changer shares the Alternate Form birthright — a human-passing form, an overtly bestial hybrid combat form, and a full beast form — and a Feral Tell, some animal marker (eyes, gait, teeth, scent) that the passing form can minimize but never fully erase. They cannot be surprised while aware; they are also baited through that Tell.

The lines. Changers run in subtype families, each a different animal instinct made flesh: the Wolf (pack hunter — strength and the hunt), the Rat (survivor and infiltrator — the gutter's own), the Feline (ambush predator — the pounce from the dark), the Reptile (cold endurance — the patient coil), and the Avian (scout and skirmisher — the eye from on high). Two more families are held in reserve. Culture & place in the world. Changers do not have one culture; they have as many as they have lines and origins, bound by a shared experience of not quite passing. In the megacities a Changer is a walking contradiction — human enough to hold a SIN, beast enough to be hunted when the Tell shows — so many run in tight kin-packs that blur the line between family, gang, and hunting party. Some corps prize engineered Changers as living infiltration and tracking assets; the occult and dimensional strains are more often feared as monsters or courted as recruits by both sides of the war. On a crew a Changer is versatility incarnate: the face who becomes the scout who becomes the beast that ends the fight.

Revenants — The Undying

Revenants - the undying — Ghostwire AI (AI-generated)

Names: Homo mortuus redivivus · Reanimate / Post-Mortem Type · Revs, Deaders, Rotters, Ghosts (late-stage). Kind: made (no one is born a Revenant — they are the returned dead). Origin & nature. No one starts life as a Revenant. They are made in the moment of death: a person who died with a purpose too fierce to release — vengeance, an oath, a debt, a flat refusal — and rose again, sustained by will rather than blood, keeping the memories and personality of the life they left. In this setting the Cosmic War supercharges that return: the Light may send a soul back to finish holy work, the Dark One may deny a soul its rest out of spite, or a corp's resurrection-tech may fail in a way that is really something older reaching through the tear. A Revenant begins as embodied undead and only slowly loses the flesh.

The Decay and the dread. A Revenant's body is a countdown. Over a career they walk a Decay ladder — from Fleshbound (a rotting, cold-fleshed corpse that walks) to Withered/Skeletal (dried toward hardened bone) to Spectral (translucent, phasing, ghostlike) — trading a little humanity at each rung for a little more of the grave's power, until the late-stage Revenant is nearly a wraith. Their Undying Return means a felled Revenant does not die but drops inert and rises again after a respite — which makes them relentless, and terrifying to fight. But it is not true immortality: fire taken while inert, consecrated or annihilating force meant to lay the dead to rest, or the deliberate destruction of the inert body ends them for good. This is why fire is a Revenant's oldest fear, and why an enemy who knows what they are facing brings a torch. Culture & place in the world. Revenants have no homeland and no bloodline — they are recruited from every other people by death itself — so their "culture" is one of purpose and unfinished business. They are walking proof that in this war death is not final, which makes them holy to some Light-orders (a soul granted a second chance) and abominations to others (a thing that should be laid to rest); the Dark One's cults covet them as recruits already halfway across. Corps that dabble in resurrection-tech both create them and hunt them. Every Revenant is a story with its last chapter unwritten — the ideal crew member with a reason, and the ideal antagonist who will not stop coming.

Mutants — The Marked

Mutants - the marked — Ghostwire AI (AI-generated)

Names: Homo sapiens aberrans · Aberrant / Mutagenic Type · Muties, Tainted, Wrongborn. Kind: made or born-marked — but never a clean bred people; always carries the taint. (See also Ch. 5, corruption, and the Founding note that some Mutant lines are failed or discarded engineered stock.) Origin & nature. A Mutant is human clay the world has rewritten — by inherited taint, by a birth in a corrupted zone, by a magical accident, an infernal bargain, or deliberate corp gene-forging. Born or made, there is no difference: every mutation is, at root, a wound the world left in a body that the body turned into a weapon. Some Mutant strains are older than any individual — the Founding note is explicit that a fraction of Mutant-kind are failed, discarded, or corrupted lines of the same thousand-year-old engineering that made the Elvani beautiful and the Corran strong: castes that came out wrong, and were culled or cast into the

Sinks to breed among themselves. Others are freshly touched last week. All of them share one thing. The Corruptive Flaw. Every Mutant carries a permanent Corruptive Flaw — the price of their power, and the setting's clearest fingerprint of the Dark One on ordinary flesh. The Flaw deepens as the Mutant leans into their gifts (a hidden Corruption Load that rises with every serious mutation), scaling from a Latent quirk, to a Manifest visible burden, to an Ascendant danger where the Dark's hand shows openly and control itself must be rolled for. This is the tragic engine of the species: power and corruption are the same current, and the more a Mutant reaches for one the more they drink of the other. A Mutant is never just a monster — most are victims of a war fought across generations, bearing a stain they never chose. Culture & place in the world. Mutants are feared as monsters, hunted as threats, hidden by their own kind in undercity enclaves, or forged on purpose by corps as expendable bio-assets — and where they stand in society tracks almost exactly with how visible and how deep their taint runs. Loose strains (Brute, Aberrant, Tainted, Latent) give them concept-families rather than true castes, because mutation is chaotic by nature and refuses to be sorted. The Dark One's cults revere powerful Mutants as chosen vessels; Light-orders meet them with pity, suspicion, or crusading steel. On a crew a Mutant is raw, escalating power with a cost the whole table can see coming — the friend who is always one bargain away from becoming the thing they fight.

Elvani — The Aesthetic Caste

Elvani - the aesthetic caste — Ghostwire AI (AI-generated)

Names: Homo sapiens gracilis ("slender/graceful") · Aesthetic-Class Engineered Type · Elves, corp-dolls, Prettyboys, Pointers, Highborn. Kind: bred (a Founding caste; breeds true, cannot interbreed). Origin & nature. The ancestor-corps engineered the Elvani to be seen: the faces of the boardroom, the media suite, the diplomatic table, and the pleasure-tiers — a bespoke aristocracy the old wealthy could literally commission. Slender, striking, unnervingly graceful, quick, commanding, and slow to age, they were the vanity caste made flesh. A thousand years on they are a fully distinct people with their own high culture — salons, patron-houses, exacting social codes — and one crucial, deliberate truth: their beauty and charm are engineered, not magical. An Elvan's "glamor" is poise and pheromone and perfect bearing, not sorcery; they cast no better than anyone, and they are happy to let others forget the difference. Their

signature is Ephemeral Grace — the twinned gift of a charm that lands like truth and a body that nothing quite catches. Long-lived, not deathless. The Elvani are Ageless in the engineered sense: their physiology resists aging and preserves youth for centuries. They are not immortal — violence, disease, drain, and eventually extreme old age still take them, and they die like anyone else; they simply take a very long time to do it (contrast the Revenant's made undeath, Ch. 15, which is the only true "deathlessness," and even that ends in fire). A several-hundred-year lifespan is advantage enough: an Elvan can outwait a rival's whole career, and — because they breed true and forget nothing — an Elvani grudge or debt can outlast the humans who first incurred it. Culture & place in the world. The Elvani sit at the top of the corporate social ladder and are never quite allowed to forget who put them there: adored and objectified, elevated and owned, a status symbol before a person. That gilded cage breeds patron intrigue, blackmail-webs dressed as salons, and the occasional beautiful runner who walks away from everything the world told them they were for. Their contempt for the Corran as "brute labor" is canon and mutual — the two engineered castes, cut from the same act a thousand years apart in station, despise each other on sight. The overtly Elvani conglomerate is Argent Exchange (Ch. 8), where this whole caste-legacy becomes present-day corporate power. A disgraced or discarded Elvan is fertile ground for the Dark One's whisper that real freedom is power, not patronage.

Corran — The Labor Caste

Corran - the labor caste — Ghostwire AI (AI-generated)

Names: Homo sapiens fossor ("delver/digger") · Corran / Labor-Class Engineered Type · Squats, Deepers, dust-eaters. Kind: bred (a Founding caste; breeds true, cannot interbreed). Origin & nature. The ancestor-corps engineered the Corran as the laborer breed — compact, immensely strong and hardy, built to work the deep mines, the cramped service crawls, the high-pressure and low-clearance spaces machines couldn't reach and baseline humans couldn't survive. They read as dwarves in build and constitution but stripped of the old fantasy trappings: no universal beards, no rune-magic birthright — just Corran men and women, proud and practical, engineered to endure and not go down. Their signature is Unyielding: the immovable laborer who refuses to be pushed, pulled, knocked down, or budged.

Culture & place in the world. A thousand years on the Corran are a fully distinct people with their own communities, dialects, and above all guild-clans — the tight, loyal work-crew-families that double as information networks and safehouse chains a crew ignores at its peril. The megacorps still read them as low-class — "just labor" — and the Corran repay it with deep solidarity, a very long memory, and a chip on the shoulder the size of a mine cart. Because they breed true and forget nothing, a Corran feud or debt runs for generations. They sit at the bottom of the corp class ladder and know it, which makes them natural runners, union agitators, undercity power-brokers, and reluctant heroes with real grievances — and fertile recruiting ground for both a Light-faith that prizes endurance and loyalty, and a Dark One who offers power to the perpetually overlooked. Their mutual contempt with the Elvani (Ch. 17) is a ready-made table tension.

Goliar — The Heavy Caste

Goliar - the heavy caste — Ghostwire AI (AI-generated)

Names: Homo sapiens giganticus ("giant") · Goliar / Heavy-Class Engineered Type · Ogres, slabs, Wallbreakers, Big-uns, Grunts. Kind: bred (a Founding caste; breeds true, cannot interbreed). Origin & nature. The ancestor-corps engineered the Goliar as the heavy breed — towering slabs of muscle built for hazardous heavy industry, demolition, load-bearing, and security/enforcement work no baseline human could survive and no Corran was big enough to do. Where the Corran are compact and unbreakable, the Goliar are enormous and overpowering — the most physically front-loaded people in the world. Their signature is Towering Menace: large size and long reach, crushing might, and a bulk so intimidating it turns their blunt manner into fear-based social power.

Culture & place in the world. A thousand years on the Goliar are a fully distinct people with their own communities, kinship-crews, and a hard-won culture of loyalty, plain speech, and slow-burning pride. The corps still deploy them as muscle — bouncers, breachers, bodyguards, riot-line — and still underestimate them as "just grunts," mistaking a slow tongue for a slow mind, which is a mistake made exactly once. Their loyalty runs deep and their memory of who treated them like people and who treated them like equipment runs deeper — fertile ground for both the Light's message of dignity and the Dark One's promise of power to the used-up. A Goliar crew-boss commands a respect no corp badge can buy, and their plain-spoken honesty in a world of liars makes them either the most trusted member of a crew or the one who never sees the double-cross coming. The sight of an angry Goliar coming through the wall ends most negotiations early.
